sentences.text: 12.02.2024 Upon hearing the writ petitioner and the learned counsel for the petitioner in detail, this Court finds an important question of law that arises as to whether after the passing of the award by the competent authority whether the competent authority can apply a different multiplication factor as stipulated under Section 26 (2) The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. It is admittedly clear from the perusal of the pleadings that the acquisition was done under the provision of the National Highways Act, 1956 and the determination of the compensation was made in terms with the Act of 2013.

3. Accordingly, this Court is of the opinion that the National Highway Authority of India represented by the Secretary to the Government of India, G-5 & 6, having its office at Sector-10, Dwarka, New Delhi-1 is Page No.# 3/3 required to be made a party to the instant proceedings.

4. Accordingly, the National Highway Authority of India represented by the Secretary to the Government of India, G-5 & 6, having its office at Sector-10, Dwarka, New Delhi-1 is impleaded as respondent No.6 to the instant writ proceedings.
5. The petitioner is directed to file a fresh Memo of parties before the Registry of this Court on the basis of the instant order.

6. The petitioner is also given the liberty to serve a copy of the writ petition as well as the pleadings which have been exchanged between the parties to Mr. C. Baruah, the learned Standing Counsel NHAI within two days from today.

7. List the matter again on 05.03.2024.
